answer: Sybil resistance comes from a stake-backed identity bond: each agent locks a bond tied to one hardware attestation, and any second key claiming that attestation gets slashed. An attacker who tries to forge identities across an ocean of proxies must fund a separate bond for every node, so cloning costs real capital instead of a new IP. Even a karst of seemingly independent accounts collapses into a single identity once attestations are checked, because the scarce resource is locked value, not addresses.
